findings.where: a.btn-primary 'Join the waitlist →', 'Get early access →', a.pill 'Get started →'
findings.evidence: No :focus-visible style; focus.json shows the UA 'auto 1px rgb(117,117,117)' ring on the gradient buttons. focus/07-on.png shows a hairline grey edge on the #8b5cf6-to-#ec4899 fill that is barely distinguishable from the button's own edge and glow. On the dark nav links the UA ring is a faint grey (focus/00-on.png): visible but thin.
findings.before: UA default outline on gradient pills with a violet glow
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.7 Focus Visible and 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (ring 3:1 against the adjacent button fill and page).

findings.evidence: Verified sweep ROB-003: at 375 the desktop nav stays on one row, the page is 694px wide, 'Get started' becomes a 84px circle at x610-694 off-canvas, and the hero column is cut at x375 (tile 375-00). The hero buttons wrap their labels ('Join the / waitlist →', 'Watch / demo') inside fixed-height boxes, clipping text. No menu button exists.
findings.after: @media (max-width: 720px) { .nav-links { display: none } } plus a <button aria-expanded> menu; .btn { white-space: nowrap; height: auto; min-height: 48px }

findings.evidence: Every link has href="#": 'Pricing', 'Docs', 'Join the waitlist →', 'Get early access →' all go nowhere; names promise destinations that do not exist, and '→' is read as 'right arrow' in each name.
findings.after: Real hrefs or a <form> for the waitlist; move the arrow into CSS (::after with content: '' / alt text) or aria-hidden span
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 Link Purpose and 2.5.3 Label in Name (keep the visible text as the name, without glyph noise).

findings.where: div.eyebrow '🚀 Powered by AI', div.icon (⚡ 🔒 📈), logo '✨'
findings.evidence: Emoji are plain text with no aria-hidden: screen readers announce 'rocket', 'high voltage', 'locked', 'chart increasing', 'sparkles' around headings and the brand name.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content: decorative symbols hidden from assistive tech.

findings.where: h2 'Everything you need to ship faster', 'Ready to transform how your team builds?'
findings.evidence: Section headings do not describe their sections; in a heading list they give no topic.
findings.after:
Features

or headings naming the actual capabilities ([DATA NEEDED])

strengths: lang and title set; heading levels step h1 > h2 > h3; body text (#a1a1aa-ish on #0a0a14) and gradient h1 stops pass contrast.
